 NFL NFL week nine: Jets v Chiefs, Rams v Commanders, Broncos v Panthers and more – updates
 🏈 Bengals joint-top of AFC North with 34-17 win in Madrid
 🏈 What do the midterms mean for the NFL? | Email Graham 
 LIVE  Updated  5m ago Graham Searles Sun 8 Nov 2026 13.07 EST First published on Sun 8 Nov 2026 12.07 EST Share Key events 1h ago Preamble 
 Patrick Mahomes will look to get the Kansas City Chiefs get back to winning ways against the New York Jets at Arrowhead. Photograph: Ed Zurga/AP View image in fullscreen Patrick Mahomes will look to get the Kansas City Chiefs get back to winning ways against the New York Jets at Arrowhead. Photograph: Ed Zurga/AP Graham Searles Sun 8 Nov 2026 13.07 EST First published on Sun 8 Nov 2026 12.07 EST Share Key events 1h ago Preamble 
 4m ago 13.07 EST Broncos 0-0 Panthers 14:02, 1st quarter 
 Nix rips two deep balls as the Broncos try and pick on the Panthers’ weak defense. The first one to Courtland Sutton is incomplete but the second forces a 27-yard gain via a pass interference penalty. The game plan is clear already. Throw, throw, throw some more. Makes sense considering their struggles running the ball. The Broncos move it into the red zone quickly.
 Share 7m ago 13.04 EST Broncos 0-0 Panthers 14:56, 1st quarter 
 Here we go! Carolina kick it away to Denver. The Broncos run it back to the 45-yard line. Nice trot from Sean Fresch. Excellent field position for Bo Nix to go to work.
 Share 13m ago 12.58 EST In more QB news Shadeur Sanders is starting for the Browns and Joe Milton for the Eagles. Happy news if you are starting opposition defenses in fantasy.
 Share 14m ago 12.56 EST Ja’Marr Chase’s touchdown in Madrid means he joins Randy Moss to be the only players in NFL history with at least seven touchdown catches in each of their first six seasons. Not bad company to keep.
 Share 21m ago 12.49 EST The Panthers meanwhile are top of the weird NFC South on 3-4 and looking to bounce back from two successive defeats.
 Share 23m ago 12.47 EST The Broncos are in Panthers country looking for a fifth successive win as they keep finding a way with their unique brand of gritty football.
 They won ugly last week with a dramatic goalline stand to deny the Kansas City Chiefs and cap their comeback from an 11-point deficit to win 28-24. It would mean they have now won 15 straight regular season games decided by one score, tied with the 2008-09 Indianapolis Colts for the longest streak in history. What’s more, it marked Bo Nix’s 13th fourth-quarterback comeback win, the most by a quarterback in his first three seasons since 1950.
 With running back JK Dobbins struggling, the Broncos have unearthed a new asset out of the backfield in fourth-round rookie Jonah Coleman, who had 104 yards and one touchdown from 15 scrimmage touches against the Chiefs.
 Share 34m ago 12.37 EST Final score: (6-2) Cincinnati Bengals 34-17 Atlanta Falcons (3-6)
 And that’s the end of that chapter. Cincinnati’s league-best passing attack was just far too much for Atlanta to handle. These Bengals look destined for the playoffs.
 View image in fullscreen Ja'Marr Chase celebrates scoring the Bengals' first touchdown with teammate Tee Higgins. Photograph: Oscar J Barroso/AFP7/Shutterstock Share 45m ago 12.25 EST PICK! Bengals 31-17 Falcons 3:54, 4th quarter 
 That is the ball game at the Bernabéu. Needing three scores Michael Penix gets desperate and throws it straight at Barrett Carter who snaffles up the interception and with it the W. Cincinnati are heading to the top of the AFC North with Pittsburgh as they both sit 6-2.
 Share Updated at  12.41 EST 50m ago 12.21 EST The big injury news is that Myles Garrett returns for the Rams on defense. If the game wrecking defensive end is at full strength then the Commanders and Jayden Daniels could be in for a very rough afternoon. Garrett’s addition is a timely boost after the Rams lost Jaylen Watson for the reminder of the season with a shoulder injury.
 Elsewhere the Cowboys are without star receiver George Pickens and cornerback Joey Porter Jr.
 Share 1h ago 12.12 EST Bengals 31-17 Falcons 7:57, 4th quarter 
 Oh my the Bernabéu looks beautiful doesn’t it? Inside the stadium Atlanta have the ball at their seven-yard line. And after a failed check down to Bijan Robinson they’re back at their four-yard line. Another couple of failed plays and the Falcons are punting. A huge failure after their defense managed to stop a visibly frustrated Joe Burrow.
 Speaking of Burrow, he and Ja’Marr Chase have had a typically successful day. The Bengals quarterback is 23/28 for 260 yards and three touchdowns while Chase has nine receptions for 144 yards and a score.
 Share 1h ago 12.07 EST Preamble
 Hola football fans, cómo estás? At the midpoint of the season week nine is underway in Madrid with the Bengals currently beating the Falcons 31-17 . Before we see how that one finishes there are seven games coming at 12pm CST/1pm EST/6pm GMT (home teams listed second):
 (6-2) Denver Broncos v Carolina Panthers (3-4)
 (3-5) Dallas Cowboys v Indianapolis Colts (2-6)
 (2-6) New York Jets v Kansas City Chiefs (5-2)
 (5-2) Detroit Lions v Miami Dolphins (1-6)
 (5-3) Cleveland Browns v New Orleans Saints (2-5)
 (4-2-1) New York Giants v Philadelphia Eagles (2-6)
 (4-4) Los Angeles Rams v Washington Commanders (2-4-1)
 A little bit of heat is on the Chiefs today as they host the Jets off the back of a two-game losing streak. On paper they should bounce back but the offensive weapons are still lacking for Patrick Mahomes so if Geno Smith and Braelon Allen can pick up where they left off last week (290 yards and two passing touchdowns and 147 rushing yards and a score respectively) then the Jets have a serious shot at an upset.
